newsitem.title: USA: Widespread weekend rains expected in U.S. Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Widespread weekend rains expected in U.S. Midwest.

text.p: The U.S. Corn Belt should see widespread rains this weekend as a warm front runs into a slow-moving cold front but meteorologists disagreed on coverage amounts.
"Today through Tuesday, we're expecting 0.25 to 1.50 inch daily with 40 to 50 percent coverage daily," said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster with Weather Express Inc in Nebraska.

"Trying to pinpoint where it's all going to be on a given day is going to be tough," he added. "By the time it's all said and done, we should have 80 percent of the corn and soybean belt covered with 0.25 to 0.75 inch rains."
Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese-Notis, said the weekend rain events would likely bring widespread rainfall to the region with mild temperatures.

"Right now, we would be looking for 70 percent coverage of rains of 0.50 to 1.00 inch from now through Saturday from Iowa and Missouri and points eastward," Solberg said. "The southern two-thirds (of the Corn Belt) will have the best chance for rain, 0.50 to 1.50 inch, for the Sunday-Monday time frame."
He said it was difficult to pinpoint coverage for that system but said there was potential for a high percentage.

CROPCAST meteorologist David Streit said coverage would be closer to 65 percent by Monday with rains favoring the northern portions on Friday and Saturday and the eastern half of the Corn Belt on Sunday and Monday.
"We're saying 0.25 to 1.00 inch, locally heavier up to two inches, with 65 percent coverage," Streit said. "That should pretty much be over by Monday."

He said central Illinois and Indiana would have the best chance for rain on Saturday night and Sunday morning. Coverage in Illinois was expected to be around 65 or 70 percent while in Indiana it was estimated at closer to 75 percent, Streit said.
